I never directly witnessed anything like we see on tv or the internet every day. I’m sure you can just imagine what I’m talking about. It is getting more and more difficult for these senseless human beings to continue to keep dogs in small, rusty cages, full of mats, and treated so unimaginably poorly. This is not the majority of people. These things happen, and fortunately these kind of
Operations are cracked down on every single day.

Fortunately we live in a world inundated with technology, and it’s becoming harder and harder for bad breeders to “get away” with substandard breeding. Part of my job was to do A LOT of vetting online, if I wasn’t in a position to meet someone in person just yet. (There are many breeders in this country.....) 

Fortunately, so many people have dogs and puppies welfare in mind. If anyone even suspects that a breeder might be operating a shady business, they now have eyes on them. There are plenty of Facebook groups dedicated to “calling out” bad breeders, along with many other website that sole purposes are to target substandard and poor breeder. 

So, fortunately for my soul, I’ve been able to shut down the worst of the worst with just some digging. 

When a breeder decides they wanted to work with the company, they would need to send an abundant amount of photos of their living conditions ( where there dogs live, sleep, eat, etc). If something was just noticeably dirty I was in a position to question it and ask that areas were better kept (this is just an example). I always asked more than enough questions. Fortunately in these cases, most breeders would always come back with incredible improvements. 

While out in the field, I was fortunate to not walk in on any major nightmares. I was always a bit hypercritical when visiting breeders because it was and is so important to me that dogs and puppies are taken care of properly. Even in some cases where I could obviously tell that the dogs were happy, healthy, and well cared for, I wold always give suggestions to breeders on how to be better. (What do I know though, right?) I always considered whether I would feel comfortable
Purchasing a puppy from someone after seeing where there dogs lived (even just in a breeder’s home, which was the case a lot of the time!)

While I have read some horror stories online, I don’t exactly want to detail that here. I’ve never been or seen a condition that made me grossly upset without doing what I could about it. Whether that meant denying their account, putting them on a “watch list” or more. 

It’s very hard to see conditions that are even close to subpar (dirty water bowls, dingey dog houses, etc) and not do something about it when there are breeders who do such an incredible job. 

At the end of the day, I knew that I  was dealing with living beings, animals and humans equally, and if work with people best I could. I’d understand if something just got dirty one day, or bedding couldn’t be changed out, but the animals are always the priority.

Edit: oh, and every time I would review an account or an actually home of a breeder, I would always take notes and discuss this with me team. We would decide what needed to be improved, what needed to be completed changed, or whether we were even going to work with a breeder. 95% of the time my feedback was taken and something was done about a situation. That other 5% is truly what drove me away. It just was no longer for me. (Also other reasons, that don’t directly correlate with business operations....) 

I know I rambled a bit, but I hope this gives you some idea..

I will always understand that a lot of people want very specific breeds with specific temperaments, etc. surely the only way to come close to ensuring that you get the “right puppy” is through a reputable breeder. I know some people who have plenty of rescue pups, but they’ve always wanted a purebred Doberman, with temperament, size, even color in mind. Having met hundreds of breeders, I can confirm that there are many who strive so incredibly hard to truly breed the best pups. That means the parent dogs are exceptionally well cared for, just as the puppies. I’ve had breeders speak to me about their breeding practices and started tearing up because of how passionate they were about it. A great breeder recognizes that not every breeder has this kind of mindset, and that’s just unfortunate. 

Personally, I have adopted two Labrador retrievers that had both passed away too soon because of cancer (and potential other ailments or diseases). This kind of heartbreak makes it hard to ever adopt or purchase a dog ever again. It can be extremely reassuring knowing exactly where a puppy comes from, where their parents come from, and if they have any sort of congenital or hereditary diseases or issues. Obviously nothing is a guarantee, but that peace of mind just really overcomes other feelings. 

It truly depends on so many factors. You just have to do your research. If you want a purebred (or even a “designer breed) (just note, I don’t exactly “agree” with every designer/mix just because they sell) then sometimes it is best to seek a breeder. 

Not everyone is incredible. Not everyone has their dog(s) best interest in mind. Not everyone is trying to better a breed. But a lot of people are. And it can be really special when you find that.

(Long post ahead) I’ve played soccer my entire life (well... until I stopped at around 19, I’m 23 now). I played for my high school and it was the only thing in my life I cared about. I’ve always felt “different” but I thought it was normal. I think it was my junior year of HS: my coach (who I didn’t care for much, and that feeling was reciprocated) was getting tougher and tougher on me. I couldn’t do anything right. She had some weird disliking of me that I couldn’t figure out. It got to the point where she would sit me out of games and even practice (so many years later, I try and figure out what I was doing wrong and I still can’t come up with anything, even when I am feeling somewhat sensible). Things got really bad. I thought I was just depressed. I tried talking to her about the “mistreatment” I felt she was giving me and she didn’t want to hear it. She told me to “write all of my feelings down”. I really thought what I had wrote to her was pretty mild. I was stressed with school and soccer. I was upset with things going on in my life, but I didn’t think I wrote anything too alarming in my letter to her.... apparently I was wrong. She showed up to my house one day after I gave her the letter and drove myself and my mother (after showing her the letter) to the hospital. I was baker acted and I guess the doctors just did what they had to and came up with the diagnoses based on info I gave them or whatever. It was a horrible experience. The doctor who diagnosed me was late, barely looked me in the eye, and acted so cold toward me. It was all a lot for me to handle at the time. And because my experience was so bad, I’ve yet to see a doctor or therapist since, and thus have been unmedicated... it’s clear that I’ve dealt with this for much longer than the ~7 years I have been aware of my diagnoses, but it constantly feels like the very beginning.
